title: Axum server skeleton with health check endpoint
user_story: As an operator, I need to run `./hookbin serve` and have a working HTTP server with a health check so I can verify the deployment is alive and monitoring tools can probe it.
description: Wire everything together: main.rs parses CLI with clap, loads config, opens the database, builds the Axum router with shared AppState, and starts the Tokio server. The health check endpoint returns 200 with a JSON body including version, uptime, and database status. Structured logging with tracing is initialized. This is the 'it boots' milestone — after this, `cargo run -- serve` produces a working server.

acceptance_criteria.then: the server starts, logs a startup message with the bound address, and accepts connections
the response is 200 with JSON body: `{"status": "ok", "version": "<cargo version>", "uptime_seconds": <n>}`

acceptance_criteria.when: sending a request to an undefined route
acceptance_criteria.then: the response is 404 with a structured JSON error (not Axum's default plain text)
structured log output includes timestamp, level, and message fields
it holds the Database, Config, and a start_time for uptime calculation
graceful shutdown occurs and the process exits cleanly
integration test uses axum::test to verify the health endpoint returns 200 with expected JSON structure
